solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Woodwind instruments? Or a brass one of note

blocks.note: a small brass instrument like a trumpet
the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A quiz question wondering whether an instrument belongs in the woodwind or the brass section of an orchestra.
explanation.walkthrough: CORNET plus TI gives CORNETTI. The question mark flags that the brass word will build a woodwind answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A cornetto is a Renaissance wind instrument blown through a cup mouthpiece but made of wood with finger holes; its plural is Italian.

clue.text: Company and troops entertain together

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for company
a host is an army or great multitude

explanation.surface: A business and a detachment of soldiers jointly laying on hospitality.
explanation.walkthrough: HOST in its old sense of an army supplies the troops.
explanation.definitionFit: To cohost is to act jointly as hosts, sharing the job of welcoming guests at an event or show.

clue.text: Remuneration when cheque writer turned up

indicators.note: in a down clue, 'turned up' flips the word so it reads from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: the person who draws, or writes, a cheque

explanation.surface: Payment arriving once the person who wrote the cheque finally shows up.
explanation.walkthrough: The banking term for whoever writes a cheque is the DRAWER; turned up it reads REWARD.
explanation.definitionFit: A reward is money or something else given in return for service, a close synonym of payment.

clue.text: Earl declared given property

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for earl
declared means said or announced

explanation.surface: A nobleman announcing that he has been handed some land.
explanation.walkthrough: E plus STATED gives ESTATED.
explanation.definitionFit: Estated is an old adjective for someone endowed with an estate, meaning land or other possessions.

clue.text: The Royal Marines love numerical data used for keeping temperature steady

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase standing for the plural noun: devices used for this

blocks.note: taken as written
standard abbreviation for the Royal Marines
love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter
short for statistics

explanation.surface: Military men who adore figures deployed to keep conditions stable.
explanation.walkthrough: THE + RM + O + STATS; the Royal Marines are a British naval infantry corps.
explanation.definitionFit: Thermostats are devices that switch heating or cooling on and off automatically to hold a set warmth.

clue.text: Native American with little time to peddle

blocks.note: a mo is a moment, a short while
to hawk goods is to sell them in the street

explanation.surface: A trader with only a moment to sell his wares.
explanation.walkthrough: MO is British informal for a moment, as in 'wait a mo'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mohawk are an Iroquoian people of New York State and Canada, so one of them is a person of that nation.

clue.text: A policeman or a senior serviceman

blocks.note: a police constable is addressed as this
a commissioned member of the armed forces holding rank

explanation.surface: Someone trying to decide whether a uniformed figure is police or military.
explanation.walkthrough: The same word covers both uniforms.
explanation.definitionFit: The title applies to any police constable and to anyone holding a commission in the army, navy or air force.

clue.text: Nurse may inadvertently cause an artery’s dilation

indicators.note: something done by accident is done carelessly, so the letters fall out of order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A warning that a careless nurse might harm a patient's blood vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: NURSE MAY rearranges to ANEURYSM; the medical surface keeps the anagram hard to spot.
explanation.definitionFit: An aneurysm is a bulge in a weakened blood-vessel wall, a swelling or widening of the vessel.

clue.text: Wanting a sound massaging

indicators.note: 'a sound' asks for a word as it is heard, not as it is written

blocks.note: wanting means lacking or requiring

explanation.surface: Someone in need of a good rub.
explanation.walkthrough: NEEDING said out loud is KNEADING; the K is silent.
explanation.definitionFit: Kneading is pressing and working muscles with the hands, like dough, which is what a masseur does.

clue.text: Artillery piece with zero problems

indicators.note: letters with problems are in trouble, so they are disordered

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A cannon reported to be in perfect working order.
explanation.walkthrough: WITH ZERO rearranges to HOWITZER; 'zero problems' reads as a phrase, hiding the indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: A howitzer is a short cannon firing shells on a high trajectory, one kind of big gun.

clue.text: Degenerate fair after inaugural Easter festival

indicators.note: inaugural means opening, so take the start of each of the next two words
the fair word comes after the two opening letters in the answer

blocks.note: the opening letters of these two words
a fete is an outdoor fair or bazaar

explanation.surface: A disreputable fair held just after the first Easter festivities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Easter festival' looks like one thing, but only its two initials are used, before FETE.
explanation.definitionFit: Effete means feeble, worn out and decadent, which matches degenerate as an adjective.

clue.text: Level of society where loose women turn on upper-class male

indicators.note: the women turn round, so their word is read backwards

blocks.note: tarts is slang for promiscuous women
U is the old label for upper-class usage
standard abbreviation for male

explanation.surface: A social set in which promiscuous women round on a posh man.
explanation.walkthrough: TARTS reversed is STRAT, then U for upper-class and M for male.
explanation.definitionFit: A stratum is a layer, and in sociology a class or rank within a population.

clue.text: Novel cure led to being affected by open sores

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters make something new

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An experimental treatment that left patients with sores.
explanation.walkthrough: CURE LED rearranges to ULCERED; the medical surface disguises 'Novel' as an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: An ulcer is an open lesion on skin or membrane, so being ulcered means having such lesions.

clue.text: A French shopping centre, opening early for expert, can’t be beaten

indicators.note: the opening of the word 'early' is its first letter

blocks.note: the French masculine word for a
a mall is a covered shopping precinct
its first letter
able means skilled or competent

explanation.surface: A French mall that opens early for experts and is unbeatable.
explanation.walkthrough: UN + MALL + E + ABLE; 'can't be beaten' means cannot be hammered into shape, not undefeatable.
explanation.definitionFit: A malleable metal can be hammered thin without breaking, so an unmalleable one resists being worked that way.

clue.text: Free from restraint, Diana’s instant messaging the jail

blocks.note: Di is short for Diana, plus the possessive S
standard abbreviation for instant messaging
a jail is a prison

explanation.surface: A campaigner using online messages to get Diana released from jail.
explanation.walkthrough: DI'S + IM + PRISON gives the rare verb DISIMPRISON.
explanation.definitionFit: To disimprison is an old verb meaning to release someone from confinement, the opposite of locking them up.

clue.text: Swank — crazy rag bag, right?

indicators.note: crazy means disordered, so these letters are scrambled

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
standard abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A show-off dismissing a shabby bag of clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: RAG BAG rearranged, then RT; 'Swank' looks like a verb but is the noun for a person.
explanation.definitionFit: A swank, in informal usage, is a person who shows off, the same as a boastful person.

clue.text: Stains shoes with carbon insert

indicators.note: the element is to be inserted into the footwear word

blocks.note: open summer shoes
chemical symbol for carbon

explanation.surface: Footwear marked with soot rubbed into it.
explanation.walkthrough: C goes into SANDALS after the first letter. 'Stains' is a noun, blots on a reputation.
explanation.definitionFit: A stain on someone's character is a disgrace, and a public disgrace is a scandal.

clue.text: Secret place for developing containers

indicators.note: something developing changes form, so the letters take a new shape

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A hidden darkroom where photographic film is developed.
explanation.walkthrough: SECRET PLACE rearranges to RECEPTACLES; the darkroom picture makes 'developing' look photographic.
explanation.definitionFit: A receptacle is any vessel or holder that receives and keeps things, the same idea as a box or tub.

clue.text: Overcome quiet clergyman with worry

blocks.note: p for piano, quiet in music
short for reverend
to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: A peaceful vicar overwhelmed by anxiety.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overcome' reads as passive in the surface but is the active verb meaning win.
explanation.definitionFit: To prevail is to triumph or win through, beating whatever opposition stands in the way.

clue.text: Ruler’s fruity wife

blocks.note: surface: a monarch's spouse with a saucy, flirtatious manner
setter's reading: the eastern consort shares her title with a dried grape

explanation.surface: Gossip about a monarch's racy consort.
explanation.walkthrough: The word is both the wife of a Muslim sovereign and a pale seedless raisin, so 'fruity' points at the second sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The consort of a sultan bears the feminine title, which is also the name of a dried seedless grape used in baking.

clue.text: Live on others’ cake

blocks.note: to live as a parasite on other people's generosity
a light airy cake made with eggs

explanation.surface: Someone surviving on food other people have baked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'others'' is the end of the verb phrase, not a possessive attached to cake.
explanation.definitionFit: To sponge off people is to scrounge from them, and a Victoria sponge is a classic light bake.

clue.text: Do you see the hidden jagged ditch?

indicators.note: the answer is concealed inside the neighbouring words of the clue

blocks.note: letters running across the two words

explanation.surface: Someone pointing out a concealed rough trench.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across jagGED DITch.
explanation.definitionFit: Geddit is a jokey spelling of 'get it?', said after a pun to ask whether the listener understood.

clue.text: Wingers with great appetites

definitions.note: an adjectival phrase for a plural noun: people who eat greedily

blocks.note: winged creatures, here large seabirds
British slang for greedy eaters

explanation.surface: Wide players on a sports team who eat a great deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wingers' suggests football but means birds; the seabird's name is British slang for a greedy person.
explanation.definitionFit: Gannets are large diving seabirds famed for gulping fish, so their name is used for voracious eaters.

clue.text: Hide completely fixes in drugs

indicators.note: the fixes go in between the drugs

blocks.note: E is ecstasy, so two of them
clips fasten or fix things

explanation.surface: Concealing all your drug fixes from view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fixes' suggests doses of drugs in the surface, but here means fasteners.
explanation.definitionFit: When one body eclipses another it blocks it from sight entirely, so to eclipse is to obscure totally.

clue.text: Find three articles on special fruit

blocks.note: an, an and a are indefinite articles
standard abbreviation for special

explanation.surface: Someone told to locate three items on some special fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: The three articles stack up before S for special.
explanation.definitionFit: Ananas is the French and botanical name for the pineapple, a tropical plant crop.

clue.text: Got ex-pupil Edward to take adult in

indicators.note: Edward is to take the next pieces inside him

blocks.note: OB is old boy, a former pupil
Ted is short for Edward
A is an adult film rating
taken as written

explanation.surface: A former pupil persuading Edward to admit a grown-up.
explanation.walkthrough: The word 'in' looks like a container signal here, but it is one of the pieces going inside; OB is the British term for a school's former pupil.
explanation.definitionFit: To obtain something is to acquire or come by it, so got and obtained are past-tense synonyms.

clue.text: On Tuesday less prepared to struggle

indicators.note: prepared means worked into a new state, so the letters are rearranged
the weekday abbreviation sits on, ahead of, the rest in this across answer

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for Tuesday
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Being less ready on a Tuesday to put up a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: TU followed by LESS rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A tussle is a vigorous scuffle or fight, so as verbs both mean to grapple or strive.

clue.text: Last month a hollow appeared decaying

blocks.note: December, the final month of the year
taken as written
a dent is a hollow in a surface

explanation.surface: A hole in something that started rotting in December.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Last month' means the final month of the year, not the previous month.
explanation.definitionFit: Decadent describes a society or culture in moral decline, going downhill and rotting from within.
